issues.legal_issue: Amenities provided for a housing colony vest in a local council under a communal-property rule only when they belong to the villagers in common by custom or are administered for their common benefit as a matter of custom; public dedication alone is insufficient.
material_facts: A housing society formed a colony and provided parks, playgrounds, schools, a library, and other common amenities for its residents.
The local council claimed that the amenities vested in it and sought an injunction concerning its statutory duties in relation to them.

The council argued that the amenities had been dedicated to the public, but there was no proof that they belonged to the villagers in common, or had been administered for their common benefit, by custom.
issues.conclusion: The amenities did not vest in the local council under section 58 of the Madras Village Panchayats Act, 1950, merely because they were provided for residents or allegedly dedicated to the public. The council was not entitled to an injunction concerning those amenities.
issues.legal_principle: Section 58 provides for vesting of property or income that by custom belongs to villagers in common, or that has been administered for their common benefit as a matter of custom. The requirement of custom applies to both forms of property or income. Dedication is not a substitute for proof of custom. Section 56 separately provides for vesting of public roads, defined in section 2(20) as roads and similar ways over which the public have a right of way. No earlier cases are relied on.

rule.if: statutory_vesting_claim and not customary_common_ownership and not customary_common_administration

predicates.statutory_vesting_claim: A local council claims that property or income vests in it under a statutory rule for communal property.
predicates.customary_common_ownership: The property or income belongs to the villagers in common by custom.
predicates.customary_common_administration: The property or income has been administered for the villagers' common benefit as a matter of custom.

issues.definition: When a local council claims statutory vesting and neither customary common ownership nor customary common administration is established, the amenities do not vest in the council.
